newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota wheat planting nearly complete.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota wheat planting nearly complete.

text.p: Planting of wheat in North Dakota neared completion during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
"Dry weather during the week allowed growers to make substantial planting progress. However, planting of potatoes, soybeans and sunflowers remained slightly behind average," the report said.
Spring wheat was 94 percent planted, ahead of 79 percent last week, 78 last year and the five-year average of 89 percent.
Spring wheat condition was rated 74 percent good to excellent, 24 percent fair and two percent poor.
Spring wheat emerged 64 pct vs 38 w/a, 44 y/a, 70 avge.
Durum wheat planted 92 pct vs 72 w/a, 75 y/a, 85 avge.
Durum wheat emerged 50 pct vs 27 w/a, 34 y/a, 61 avge.
Oats planted 96 pct vs 83 w/a, 76 y/a, 87 avge.
Oats emerged 60 pct vs 35 w/a, 39 y/a, 68 avge.
Corn planted 93 pct vs 78 w/a, 74 y/a, 85 avge.
Corn emerged 56 pct vs 28 w/a, 34 y/a, 55 avge.
Soybeans planted 72 pct vs 45 w/a, 39 y/a, 76 avge.
Soybeans emerged 25 pct vs 3 w/a, 8 y/a, 41 avge.
Sugarbeets planted 99 pct vs 93 w/a, 89 y/a, 97 avge.
Sugarbeets emerged 56 pct vs 37 w/a, 61 y/a, 87 avge.
Sunflowers planted 13 pct vs 1 w/a, 1 y/a, 19 avge.
